title: How do we order the points from highest to lowest?
description: The seven heights of the cross section are sorted into a list from the greatest to the least, and then the list is turned around. Positive heights come first, then the negative ones with the one nearest to zero first. The slip of putting minus twelve hundred before minus two hundred is shown.
teaching_notes: One idea: a decreasing order starts with the greatest number, and among negative numbers the one nearest to zero is the greater. Watch for students who put minus twelve hundred above minus two hundred because twelve hundred is the bigger number.

video_script.why: The child orders seven signed heights from the greatest to the least and then from the least to the greatest.
video_script.substitution: The book's own cross section with points A to G, using the heights already read from it.
video_script.anchor: the geographical cross section of the book, with a height scale in metres and the sea level line at zero
video_script.payoff_line: Among negative numbers, the one nearest to zero is the greatest.

final_answer.value: Decreasing: A, E, C, G, F, B, D. Increasing: D, B, F, G, C, E, A.
final_answer.spoken: decreasing order is eigh, E, C, G, F, B, D, and increasing order is D, B, F, G, C, E, eigh

hold_back: Decreasing: A, E, C, G, F, B, D. Increasing: D, B, F, G, C, E, A.
maths_rules: heights read from the picture (approximate): A = +1500, E = +1200, C = +300, G = +100, F = -200, B = -500, D = -1200 (metres)
every positive number is greater than 0 and every negative number is less than 0
among positive numbers, the larger number is greater
among negative numbers, the one nearer to 0 is greater: -200 > -500 > -1200
decreasing order: A, E, C, G, F, B, D; increasing order is the same list turned around: D, B, F, G, C, E, A
video_script.design: The same cross section with seven heights beside the points. The points slide into a row on a number line, teal for positive and amber for negative.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>The book asks us to line up the seven points by height.
Which point should come first when we go from the highest to the lowest?

<bookmark mark='zero'/>The height at sea level is zero metres.
<bookmark mark='sign'/>A place above sea level has a positive height. A place below sea level has a negative height.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Among negative numbers, the one nearest to zero is the greatest.
